source.title: Principled Synthetic Data Enables the First Scaling Laws for LLMs in Recommendation
source.authors: Ben-Yu Zhang; Qiang Zhang; Jianpeng Cheng; Hong-You Chen; Qi-Fei Wang; Wei Sun; Shen Li; Jia Li; Jia-Hao Wu; Qun-Shu Zhang; Neeraj Bhatia; Xiang-Jun Fan; Hong Yan

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figure content and tables are flattened or garbled in the extracted text; the reported text and legible table values are used where assignable.
record.tranche_reason: It measures scaling-law behavior in a new setting: continual pre-training for recommendation using synthetic recommendation data, with additional experiments on a proprietary social-media recommendation dataset.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study's own held-out perplexity/loss scaling fits, computed allocation trade-offs, data-mixture and repetition experiments, and reported downstream correlation. The TSTR-versus-TRTR sequential recommender comparison is not a test of scaling with model size, data, or compute; prior-work results such as PLUM are cited context, not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study fits saturating power laws of held-out loss/perplexity against training tokens and parameters. It does this for continual pre-training (CPT) of Qwen3 and Gemma-3 on synthetic recommendation data, with repeated-data and data-mixture variants. This is a new training regime with its own results on whether the power-law form holds (V5) and on how fits depend on setup (V7). It does not pretrain from scratch, so V1 is not directly tested. V3 allocation is only derived analytically from the fitted law, so V3 is not tested empirically.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors claim that position-debiased synthetic curricula enable the first robust power-law scaling for LLM CPT in recommendation. They report a data-efficiency hierarchy (UIH > CF > Item-Text > General) and asymmetric CF→UIH transfer. They frame compute allocation as domain-dependent, model-dominant for text and data-dominant for UIH. They also acknowledge overfitting beyond ~16 repeats and inverse size scaling on UIH OOD, which they attribute to memorization of repeated data.
record.recipe_differences: Uses power-law fits to held-out evaluation loss/perplexity against training tokens and model size, but applies them to Qwen3 recommendation CPT with synthetic recommendation data rather than the original general-language-model setup. It also derives allocation implications from the joint fit.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted exponents and asymptotic losses vary by evaluation domain and model size. UIH outcomes vary with data mixture and repetition; the paper reports overfitting onset at different total training-token counts for 2% versus 15% UIH mixtures. It states that the additive joint fit does not fully capture a model–data interaction. Extended social-media results differ from MerRec, including a reported UIH data exponent of 0.894 versus 0.272.

fits_no_version.finding: Sequential recommenders (GRU4Rec, NARM, STAMP, SASRec) trained on the synthetic data beat real-data training on a filtered real test set. The abstract cites +130% recall@100 for SASRec.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Synthetic graph-walk recommendation data yields better ranking recall than real logs for standard sequential recommenders.

fits_no_version.finding: Synthetic UIH has item Gini 0.635–0.732 (production config 0.639) vs >0.95 in real logs; it has no position bias by construction and keeps some popularity bias.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Graph random-walk synthetic histories reduce exposure inequality relative to real logs.

record.peer_reviewed: Accepted by ICML 2026 (as stated in the paper); venue metadata also identifies arXiv.org.
record.problems: The main scaling experiment uses four model sizes trained on the same 163B-token budget, so it does not empirically establish a compute-optimal parameter/token trajectory across budgets. The paper does not directly validate small-run extrapolations on held-out larger runs. Some extended social-media findings are reported with limited methodological detail in the supplied text. No uncertainty intervals are reported for the main fitted parameters.
record.rows_left_out: No otherwise relevant results were omitted to meet the row limit. Figure-only ranking comparisons are not scaling-law results and are noted under gate_note and fits_no_version.

untested.parts: All of it. Every run is continual pre-training from pretrained Qwen3/Gemma checkpoints, not pretraining from scratch.
No fit on small runs is checked against larger held-out runs. The 1,104B-token extension is asserted without numbers.
There is no sweep over compute budgets with measured optimal N and D. Allocation is derived analytically from the additive fit, and all main runs use one token budget.
No comparison of depth, width or other shape choices.
Image/video modalities, fine-tuning and transfer beyond recommendation CPT.
No quantified relation between loss and downstream metrics, and none on MerRec.

missing.what: Per-model fits across 0.6B–32B on reduced UIH at 2% and 15% ratios, including α=0.000 for 8B/14B/32B on UIH and the General-domain fits up to 32B
UIH Full Graph per-model fits (L∞≈0.69–0.70, α 0.555–0.689), distinct from UIH OOD
Changing the tokenizer (SAE vs RQ-kmeans, 4B) changes fitted exponents, e.g. UIH OOD α 0.564 vs 0.421 and Item-Text L∞ 0.86 vs 1.25
Per-mixture fitted α per domain, e.g. CF α=0.000 under UIH-only and Item-Text α=0 without Item-Text data
Separate CF Both Seen / One Unseen / Both Unseen fits

record.verdict_notes: Rows are relinked from V1 to V5 because all runs are CPT from pretrained checkpoints. The compute-allocation implication rests on the αA/βB coefficient ratio, not on measured optima. Under the additive fit the General-domain optimum gives N∝C^~0.09, so the growth exponents would favour data despite the 'model-dominant' label. The §9.1 claim that 'α decreases monotonically with model size' is contradicted by Table 9: General α rises 0.025→0.051 and Alignment is non-monotonic. It also conflicts with the MerRec finding that α rises with size for CF/UIH. No uncertainty is reported for the MerRec fits. Table 5 is partly garbled: the Item-Text 8B value differs between table and figure.

versions.untested_parts: The study varies training tokens and parameter count in recommendation CPT, but does not establish the original claim's full range of conditions or directly measure cross-entropy as distinct from its reported perplexity/loss metric.
No held-out test of predictions made by fitting only smaller runs and forecasting the loss of substantially larger runs.
It derives domain-specific allocation implications from fitted laws, but does not empirically sweep multiple compute budgets to show parameter and token optima each grow as a power of compute.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Tests recommendation-specific CPT and repeated synthetic-data regimes; it does not test image/video modalities, fine-tuning, or other transfer settings.
Reports a qualitative perplexity–Recall@K/NDCG correlation in extended experiments, but does not give a quantified scaling relationship or a downstream prediction test on the main MerRec experiments.

Shows dependence on domain, data mixture, and repetition, and reports that the additive joint fit misses a model–data interaction. It does not investigate parameter-counting choices or compare multiple fitting methods.

relationships.condition: Recommendation CPT with unrepeated or modestly repeated data (≤~8 repeats), Qwen3 0.6B–8B on MerRec and Qwen3/Gemma-3 on a proprietary dataset
relationships.reason: Saturating power-law fits in tokens and joint N,D fits hold across domains and two model families. The proprietary fits report RMSE<0.035. The 8B model is best on General at fixed tokens (r01–r20, r25, r28–r30, r40–r52).
relationships.display_finding: Token and joint model/data power laws held across domains and two model families, with proprietary-data RMSE<0.035; the 8B model performed best on General at fixed tokens.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Recommendation CPT with unrepeated or modestly repeated data (≤~8 repeats), Qwen3 0.6B–8B on MerRec and Qwen3/Gemma-3 on a proprietary dataset
source_check.reason: Tables 5 and 7 and §9.1 report saturating power-law data scaling in these regimes, including proprietary fits with RMSE<0.035. Support concerns the fitted scaling axes; the fixed-token UIH size reversal warrants its separate verdict.

relationships.condition: Heavily repeated UIH data (≥~16 repeats) and CF evaluation across model sizes
relationships.reason: Held-out perplexity rises after ~16 repeats at every scale, and fits for 8B–32B give α=0. CF perplexity saturates at 4B (r26, r31–r35).
relationships.display_finding: Held-out perplexity rose after approximately 16 repeats at every scale, with zero exponents for 8B–32B models, while CF perplexity saturated at 4B.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Heavily repeated UIH data (≥~16 repeats) and CF evaluation across model sizes
source_check.reason: For heavily repeated UIH, §7.2 explicitly reports increasing held-out perplexity beyond approximately 16 repeats across model sizes, and Figure 7 includes α=0 fits for 8B–32B. This is reversed or absent improvement and merits challenges. The separate CF saturation result in §7.3 should retain its own limits_scope condition rather than be combined with the repetition reversal.

relationships.condition: UIH OOD evaluation at a fixed 163.84B tokens with recommendation data repeated 6–7×
relationships.reason: Loss is reversed in model size: 0.6B scores ~2.01 PPL vs 8B at 2.10 (r27).
